question: Does defining covering as mere impurity-existence absurdly imply covering of Shiva?
premises: If covering is only the mere existence of impurity, the definition is too broad.
By that reasoning, even those of the stated nature could be said to have covering.
The definition would absurdly extend covering to Shiva.
inference: The mere-existence definition of covering leads to an absurd overextension.
plain_english: Alas, by this reasoning, even for those of the stated nature there would truly be a covering of Shiva, merely from the existence of impurity.
